public_payload.normalized_proposition: He believes Anthropic's new weekly limits on Claude Code accounts will create some of the most gnarly churn in SaaS history.
conditions: Anthropic adding weekly limits on accounts

statement.excerpt: It already has their own extremely-expensive coding environment, Claude Code, which I estimated loses the company 100% to 10,000% of a subscription per-customer a few weeks ago, and now Anthropic is adding weekly limits on accounts, which will, I believe, create some of the most gnarly churn in SaaS history.

from_speaker: Anthropic is adding weekly limits on accounts
some of the most gnarly churn in SaaS history
our_interpretation: The assessed proposition is the churn forecast. The preceding per-customer loss estimate is background, not a separate proposition graded here.
The plain reading is unusually severe cancellation of paid subscriptions used for Claude Code, caused by the new weekly limits, relative to historical SaaS experience.
“I believe” expresses confidence; it is not a separate condition.
No numerical churn threshold or observation window is imposed. Only an unambiguous historical comparison could settle the qualitative superlative.
Implementation of weekly limits is the antecedent. An announced implementation date alone would not prove it occurred.
criteria.support_condition: Representative paid-subscriber data show historically exceptional churn after implementation, with credible evidence that the weekly limits caused it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative data covering the affected subscribers and policy episode show ordinary or low churn on comparable historical SaaS measures, excluding the predicted exceptional effect.
